text: After the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus didn't walk toward the crowd. He walked toward a leper hiding among the rocks.
explanation:
A leper couldn't sit among the thousands listening on the hillside; he'd have been driven away. He must have listened from a distance, hearing words like "Your heavenly Father feeds the birds… are you not of more value than they?" Whatever he heard, it wasn't judgment. It gave him the courage to come.

He was sure Jesus could heal him, but not sure He would: "Lord, if You are willing." He never asked to be touched. Yet Jesus reached out His hand, touched the untouchable and said, "I am willing; be cleansed." The crowd had to follow Him, because He'd gone looking for one.

text: Nebuchadnezzar's statue declined from gold to silver, bronze, iron and clay. The Beloved is gold from head to foot.
explanation:
In the king's dream, the empires of the world were a great statue: a head of gold (Babylon), chest of silver (Medo-Persia), belly of bronze (Greece), legs of iron (Rome) and feet of iron mixed with clay. Each was stronger in some ways but lower in value. Everything of man starts well and deteriorates.

The bride in the Song of Songs describes her Beloved: "His head is like the finest gold… his hands are rods of gold… his legs are pillars of marble set on bases of fine gold." Gold at the head, the hands and the feet. Jesus never declines. He doesn't get sweeter over time; your view of Him does.

text: "This secret has not been revealed to me because I have more wisdom than anyone living." Daniel hid behind God's glory.
explanation:
All of Babylon's astrologers and magicians failed, and the king ordered them all executed, Daniel included. Daniel calmly asked for time, gathered his three friends to pray, and slept. That night God showed him the dream. Standing before the most powerful man on earth, Daniel said: "There is a God in heaven who reveals secrets."

Like Joseph before Pharaoh, Daniel was quick to step out of the spotlight and turn it onto God. The people God brings forward are the ones who have learned to hide behind Him. When He puts you in front, put Him in front again.

text: When Daniel and his friends sought "mercies" from God, the Hebrew word comes from the word for womb.
explanation:
Facing execution in the morning, Daniel and his friends sought "mercies from the God of heaven." The word is rachamim, related to rechem, a mother's womb: the tender compassion a mother has for the child she carries. That's how God regards you when you come to Him in prayer.

Jesus spoke the same way over Jerusalem: "How often I wanted to gather your children together, as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings." Come to Him as one held close, cherished and covered, and you can sleep at night even with a crisis waiting in the morning.

text: "For our sakes," said Daniel. God moves kings and empires for the sake of His people.
explanation:
Daniel told Nebuchadnezzar that God had revealed the dream "for our sakes." History books record empires rising and falling, but Scripture reveals why. Caesar Augustus decreed a census of the whole Roman world, thinking about taxes. God was making sure a carpenter from Nazareth and his pregnant wife were in Bethlehem at the right time.

What happens to the nations ultimately revolves around God's purposes for His people. You don't need to fear the headlines. The One who moves kings is moving with you in mind.

text: When God is your only fear, you're free from every other fear.
explanation:
In Babylon, the wise men had every resource except the one that mattered, and they had no answer. When God is pushed out, people don't end up believing nothing; they'll believe almost anything. True wisdom begins with the fear of the Lord, which means worshipping Him.

When He is the One you revere, you stop living for the opinions of others, the likes and dislikes, the next bad news report. Daniel answered with "counsel and wisdom" when everyone else was panicking. Look up first, and you'll find the calm to deal with what's around you.
